rationale:
Issue #177 ("Using `GeneralName.directoryName` results in a corrupt certificate") is traced to merged PR #188 and fix commit 387fb97 via fix_commit_to_merged_pr_to_issue. The defect is that GeneralName.directoryName treated DistinguishedName as implicitly taggable, so the [4] context tag replaced the DN's SEQUENCE tag on serialize and parse instead of wrapping it, producing a malformed encoding. The minimized patch keeps exactly the two behavioral hunks in Sources/X509/GeneralName.swift that switch the directoryName case to DER.explicitlyTagged on parse and coder.serialize(_:explicitlyTaggedWithIdentifier:) on serialize; the four unrelated hunks (DistinguishedName DERParseable/DERSerializable conformances, the deprecation annotation, and the DistinguishedName.derEncoded call-site churn in CertificationRequestInfo, CMSIssuerAndSerialNumber, TBSCertificate) were removed, and post_minimization_validation is PASS with strict_post_minimization all-green. The trigger is the unchanged upstream test testAKISerialization from the same commit; it uses only APIs present on the buggy revision (DistinguishedName result builder, AuthorityKeyIdentifierValue, DER.Serializer, and init(derEncoded:) available through the pre-existing DERImplicitlyTaggable conformance), so it compiles on both revisions, and its assertion targets the exact reported symptom: explicit 0xa4 0x39 wrapping an inner 0x30 0x37 SEQUENCE plus a round-trip equality check. Machine evidence shows trigger.buggy_differential and trigger.fixed_clean pass with 3 repetitions, buggy full-suite failures limited to the reproduced trigger, and fixed full suite green. active_same_project_root_causes is empty, so #177 is not a duplicate.

Issue 177 ('Using GeneralName.directoryName results in a corrupt certificate', closed, traced fix_commit -> merged PR 188 -> issue) describes wrong DER encoding for the directoryName CHOICE alternative. The minimized production patch keeps exactly the two behavioral hunks in Sources/X509/GeneralName.swift that switch directoryName from implicit tagging (DistinguishedName(derEncoded:withIdentifier:) / serialize(into:withIdentifier:)) to explicit tagging (DER.explicitlyTagged / serialize(_:explicitlyTaggedWithIdentifier:)), which is the ASN.1-correct encoding since DistinguishedName is itself a CHOICE-bearing SEQUENCE. The four removed hunks were the deprecation shim, the new DERParseable/DERSerializable conformances and the DistinguishedName.derEncoded call-site adaptations, i.e. API-shape work not needed to correct the symptom; nothing formatting-, doc-, config- or test-only remains. The trigger is the unchanged upstream test from the same fix commit (testAKISerialization), which uses APIs that already existed on the buggy revision (GeneralName.directoryName, the DistinguishedName result builder, AuthorityKeyIdentifierValue, DER.Serializer) and asserts both round-trip equality and the exact byte sequence 0xa4 0x39 wrapping the inner SEQUENCE, matching the reported corruption rather than any fix-only API. Strict post-minimization evidence reports build.both_versions PASS, trigger.buggy_differential reproducing only Tests/X509Tests/CertificateTests.swift::testAKISerialization, trigger.fixed_clean PASS, deterministic over 3 repetitions, and full_suite.fixed_all_green; the second declared selector testCertificateDescription is non-reproducing and passes on both revisions. active_same_same_project registry is empty, so the root cause is not a duplicate, and apple/swift-certificates#177 is in allowed_root_cause_ids.
